items.abstract: <jats:p>Few-shot industrial anomaly detection requires a reliable alarm threshold when only defect-free samples are available. Frozen visual features improve data efficiency, but a high AUROC does not itself define a deployable operating point. We propose CAL-FrozenAD, a training-free framework that fuses nearest-neighbor patch distances from texture-sensitive and semantic layers and calibrates the image score by split conformal prediction. Under exchangeable normal data, the resulting threshold controls the marginal false-alarm probability at a user-selected level; the same fused map provides pixel localization. In one-shot experiments on MVTec AD, VisA, and Real-IAD, CAL-FrozenAD reaches 80.5% mean image AUROC and 80.5% mean recall at a nominal 5% false-alarm level, improving the strongest baseline by 0.5 and 2.6 percentage points, respectively, with 1.4 ms/image additional inference time.</jats:p>
title: Calibrated few-shot industrial anomaly detection with frozen visual features

<jats:p>In industrial manufacturing, ensuring quality control is critical to maintaining high standards and operational efficiency. Manual defect detection, however, is often time-consuming, error-prone, and costly, thereby driving the need for automated solutions. This paper investigates a technique for industrial anomaly detection (IAD) by utilizing the state-of-the-art PatchCore algorithm in conjunction with the widely recognized MVTec AD dataset. The dataset consists of 5354 high-resolution color images representing diverse objects and textures, including defect-free samples for training and numerous anomalous instances for testing. With over seventy distinct defect types—such as scratches, dents, contamination, and other structural irregularities—the dataset presents substantial challenges for conventional visual inspection (VI) techniques. The approach integrates convolutional neural networks (CNNs) with patch-based feature extraction methods, enabling PatchCore to accurately identify and localize even subtle anomalies within complex industrial imagery. Experimental results demonstrate that PatchCore significantly enhances detection accuracy, reduces false positives, and streamlines the overall inspection process. These improvements have important implications for operational productivity and quality assurance in various industrial sectors, paving the way for more reliable and cost-effective manufacturing practices.

items.abstract: <jats:p>Zero-shot learning (ZSL) addresses scarce samples and unseen categories in industrial defect detection. Zero-shot multi-type anomaly segmentation (MTAS) demands both anomaly localization and fine-grained defect classification, yet mainstream methods like MultiADS face an inherent alignment-generalization paradox: they rely on static prompts and one-way alignment, failing to adapt to fine-grained visual variations and limiting accuracy.To tackle this, we propose the Dynamic Anomaly-Aware Segmentation (DAAS) framework for zero-shot industrial defect detection. Its core is a customized training-only Post-VCP module. Based on industrial defect-tailored multi-head cross-attention over local visual features, this module provides strong supervision for text embedding learning, preserves semantic priors via residual connections, and enhances the fine-grained modeling ability of static text embeddings for inference.Extensive transductive experiments on four benchmarks (MVTec-AD, VisA, MPDD, MAD-real) show DAAS achieves substantial gains on MTAS over MultiADS, with competitive results on binary ZSL. These validate our method’s effectiveness, theoretical rationality and robustness in real industrial scenarios.</jats:p>

items.abstract: Industrial visual anomaly detection (IVAD) underpins automated quality inspection, yet deployment is constrained by scarce target-domain data, rare defects, and frequent distribution shifts. Foundation models supply reusable semantic, spatial, and reasoning priors for cold-start IVAD, but these priors are not anomaly-aware, and existing studies vary in their assumptions about target samples, auxiliary data, and model adaptation, hindering fair comparison. This survey reviews foundation-model-based IVAD under a deployment-oriented cold-start formulation. We separate target-domain data availability from auxiliary-data adaptation, distinguishing zero-shot, few-normal, and few-abnormal regimes, and organize methods by their role in the inspection pipeline: preprocessing and region-of-interest grounding, structural anomaly localization, and logical anomaly reasoning. We summarize representative datasets, cross-dataset protocols, and evaluation metrics, emphasizing how data assumptions affect reported performance. Finally, we discuss open challenges in scalable deployment, anomaly-aware adaptation, fine-grained localization, logical reasoning, and reliable evaluation.
title: Foundation Models for Cold-Start Industrial Visual Anomaly Detection: A Survey

items.abstract: <jats:p>Industrial visual anomaly detection is crucial for ensuring system reliability, safety, and production efficiency. However, most existing methods rely on static image modeling and ignore the temporal characteristics of industrial data, making it difficult to capture subtle and dynamically evolving anomalies in complex environments. To address this issue, we propose an online industrial visual anomaly detection method based on temporal aggregation representations. This method first converts consecutive image frames into temporally ordered spatiotemporal representations using a dimension-transformation-based temporal aggregation strategy, thereby suppressing factory environmental noise and enhancing subtle anomalous features. Subsequently, a Multiscale Wavelet-based Salient Attention (MWSA) module is designed to enhance the discriminability of subtle anomalous features through low-frequency structural enhancement and high-frequency noise suppression. Building upon this, a memory bank of normal features is constructed, and anomaly detection and localization are achieved based on nearest-neighbor distances. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves high-precision visual anomaly detection and localization, while maintaining stable performance under varying camera conditions and complex industrial environments. Actual deployment results demonstrate that the method exhibits excellent environmental robustness, achieving an event-level recall rate of 94.83\% and effectively reducing false triggers caused by complex background interference, thereby providing an efficient and robust solution for quality control in industrial automation.</jats:p>
title: Online Industrial Visual Anomaly Detection Using Temporal Aggregation Representations: A Case Study of Yarn Breakage Detection in Warp Knitting

items.abstract: Industrial visual anomaly detection plays a pivotal role in ensuring product quality and operational safety across manufacturing, energy, and precision engineering sectors. However, most deep learning approaches rely on extensive defect datasets, making them unsuitable for real-world scenarios where only a single defective instance may be available. To address this challenge, this paper introduces Light-MLLMAD, a Lightweight Multimodal Large Language Model framework designed for one-shot industrial anomaly detection. The proposed model integrates a compact vision encoder with parameter-efficient adapter layers and a text-guided reasoning module, enabling efficient learning from minimal examples. By employing prompt-conditioned anomaly grounding, Light-MLLMAD leverages natural-language prompts to describe contextual attributes such as texture, color deviation, or surface irregularity, thus enhancing interpretability and localization accuracy. A contrastive embedding regularization strategy further ensures robust separation between normal and anomalous features even with limited samples. Extensive experiments conducted on benchmark datasets—covering metallic surfaces, printed circuit boards, and industrial components—demonstrate that Light-MLLMAD achieves superior detection accuracy while reducing computational cost by over 60% compared to traditional vision-language models. The system also achieves near real-time inference on edge hardware, confirming its deployability in factory settings. Overall, the proposed framework bridges the gap between multimodal reasoning and lightweight industrial implementation, offering an interpretable, resource-efficient, and scalable approach for one-shot visual anomaly detection.
title: Light-MLLMAD: A Lightweight Multimodal Large Language Model for One-Shot Industrial Visual Anomaly Detection

items.abstract: This thesis addresses deep learning-based methods for automatic anomaly detection in an industrial context. It involves image- or sensor-based detection of defects in the production process that can affect the quality of products. Automating this task provides a reliable and cost-effective alternative to humans, who perform this task manually by sighting. Since this setup has special requirements such as detecting previously unknown defects that traditional approaches cannot fulfill, this paper presents anomaly detection methods that learn without any examples of anomalies and include only normal data in the training process. Most of our proposed methods address the problem from a statistical perspective. Based on a deep-learning-based density estimation of the normal data, it is assumed that anomalies are considered unlikely according to the modeled distribution. The density estimation is performed by socalled Normalizing Flows, which, in contrast to conventional neural networks, can model a formally valid probability distribution due to their bijective mapping.
